thread.title: Close Update: Wall Street Mixed as Measures Pare Losses Before Apple, Fed

title: Close Update: Wall Street Mixed as Measures Pare Losses Before Apple, Fed
text:
Close Update: Wall Street Mixed as Measures Pare Losses Before Apple, Fed May 01, 2018, 04:19:13 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo
Wall Street was mixed on Tuesday, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average weaker for a third straight day while the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite reclaimed losses and turned positive as information technology rose ahead of key earnings from Apple ( AAPL ).
The group gained 1.5% into the close as five of the 11 sectors on the S&P ended in the green. A slide in crude prices dented the energy component while telecoms and consumer staples also retreated. Financials were slightly higher as the Federal Open Market Committee's third interest-rate meeting of 2018 got underway.
Apple rose more than 2% Tuesday but the tech giant's stock has come under pressure recently amid concerns about sales of its iPhone. The gains in the blue chip weren't enough to keep the Dow afloat amid losses in Pfizer ( PFE ) and Merck ( MRK ) after both drugmakers fell short of analysts' expectations in their quarterly revenue.
Earnings have largely come in well ahead of projections in the first quarter reporting season, with 78% beating estimates on earnings and 75% on sales as of late Monday, according to the Earnings Scout.
But issues on other fronts have also grabbed attention, with investors keeping an eye on geopolitics and the Fed as the two-day policy meeting started. While the benchmark interest rate is likely to be kept on hold, the "risk is the statement is slightly more cautious on the economic outlook given some of the slowing in data and the worries seen in the Beige Book over potential tariffs," Action Economics said in a note.
Vehicle sales for April also dented some sentiment on Tuesday, with Action projecting a 2% drop in the sales rate to about 17 million as consumers seem hesitant to convert more disposable income into higher spending. General Motors ( GM ) and Honda ( HMC ) weakened, while Ford (F) and Fiat Chrysler (FCAU) managed gains.
